column3: Directly confirms that those in the Fire cannot leave it.
Offers a present response of patience, not an afterlife reading.
Shows deeds becoming void at the meeting and without weight.
Exposes the false promise that leaders can carry followers' sins.
Addresses life and death of those killed in God's way.
Contrasts following revelation with the culpable following in 2:167.
Repeats the wish for a return in order to become believers.
Frames trial and patience, only distantly contrasting later regret.
States that people will be shown their deeds.
Immediate antecedent: leaders disown followers as punishment appears.
Gives faithful speech at calamity, not the followers' final regret.
Uses return as a losing prospect, but in a different setting.
Contains reciprocal mockery, not culpable following or final regret.
Describes mercy and guidance for the steadfast.
Names regret placed in hearts over a counterfactual claim.
Shows misleaders disowning those they led astray.
Regulates pilgrimage rites.
Concerns judgment by the revealed Book.
Links following what displeases God to deeds being nullified.
Warns of concealing guidance, without the final-scene relations.
Shows evil deeds beautified and then regarded as good, ending in regrets.
Explicitly joins seeing punishment with wishing for a return.
Shows repentance and reform before the final regret becomes fixed.
Depicts allies failing to support one another, with no final judgment scene.
Contrasts following falsehood with following truth.
Establishes curse on those who die rejecting, but not 2:167's scene.
Uses disavowal in a treaty context, not final separation.
Records false excuses for associating partners, like evading responsibility.
Immediate context: enduring punishment without relief or delay.
Those in the Fire ask to be taken out to do otherwise, too late.
Connects void deeds with abiding in the Fire.
States divine oneness, the preceding basis for rejecting rival allegiances.
Depicts unbelief with deeds made void.
Presents arrogant denial and divine superiority, not the followers' regret.
Immediate context: signs support the recognition 2:167 presumes.
Mentions showing great signs without the judgment theme.
Records shirk-based excuses and following conjecture before punishment.
Warns that associating partners nullifies deeds.
People in the Fire seek even a day's reduction of punishment.
Promises disclosure of what rejecters did and severe punishment.
The one who beautified deeds turns back and declares disavowal.
Affirms that a person's striving will be seen.
Sets a rule of permission for children.
States abiding in Hell for rejecters and associators.
Mentions deeds not being lost for those killed in God's way.
Identifies the believers who follow the Prophet.
Warns against alliances with those who turn away, without final regret.
Commands following the messenger as the alternative to misplaced following.
Portrays mutual association, acknowledgment, and abiding in the Fire.
Names the Day of Regret after the matter is decided.
Commands following rightly guided messengers, as a general contrast.
Commands following revelation rather than other protectors.
Links a return to wrongdoing with abiding in the Fire.
Concerns patience before addressing the Prophet.
Makes each party responsible for its own deeds and mutually disavowed.
Concerns a barrier against corrupters.
Explicitly voices regret over neglect before God.
Speaks of testing and God's awareness of deeds.
Depicts associates being absent when summoned, without the followers' scene.
The condemned admit sins and ask whether there is a way out.
Shows people turning away from required fighting.
Describes a community enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
Includes a counterfactual complaint, but concerns battle and hidden thoughts.
States God's knowledge of deeds, without regret or separation.
Uses return in a historical restoration, not a wish after judgment.
Describes reward and abiding for workers of good.
Concerns a decreed sign and mercy.
Affirms God's power over those promised punishment.
Warns against hardened hearts and persistent disobedience before the end.
Uses leaving and entering in a land dispute.
Links rejecting after turning back to void deeds and eternal Fire.
Mentions shown signs and denial, without the final regret.
The lack of intercessors reinforces the followers' helplessness.
Relates the night journey and signs.
Uses repeated looking and weariness, not return or final regret.
Uses following a route.
Commands sincere worship despite rejecters' dislike.
Separates a speaker from responsibility for others' deeds.
Explicitly declares disavowal from the deeds of those who disobey.
Limits following to revelation, contrasting dependent allegiance.
Names the message a regret for rejecters.
Shows signs rejected, without the consequences articulated in 2:167.
States God's establishing truth despite criminals' dislike.
States recompense for evil and good according to what was done.
Those stationed at the Fire wish to be sent back and changed.
Commands righteous work and notes God's knowledge of deeds.
Shows resulting enmity and later disclosure of deeds.
Uses God showing signs through reviving the dead.
The condemned ask to see and abase those who led them astray.
Assures the reward of good work, only a broad contrast.
A counterfactual plea for guidance parallels the too-late wish in 2:167.
Records an accusation against the messenger.
Addresses hypocrisy, distortion, and worldly and final punishment.
Describes natural signs and revival of the earth.
Shows disobedience and divided worldly or afterlife desire.
Expresses abhorrence of others' deeds.
Concerns reliance on God amid practical precautions.
Identifies following conjecture in taking alleged partners besides God.
Describes clothing of those in blessing.
States that God will observe how people act after succession.
Sets up the pericope: rivals are loved as God is loved.
Condemns following inherited ways instead of revealed guidance.
Warns that following a path other than believers leads to Hell.
Denies that any ransom can avert the Fire's punishment.
Says that, even if returned, they would resume what they forbade.
Names regret over neglect at the meeting with God.
Shows alleged partners absent when people come to God alone.
Portrays groups entering the Fire and cursing those before them.
Shows earlier groups denying later followers any relief from punishment.
Joins fulfilled warning, lost intercessors, and a wish to return.
Alleged partners disown the worship directed to them.
Shows every soul tested by what it sent ahead and false claims lost.
Weak followers confront the arrogant leaders after all appear before God.
Satan disowns those who followed his promise and assigns them blame.
Links making rivals to God with leading others from His path.
Shows misleaders carrying burdens from those they mislead.
Those who associated partners see them and their claims are rejected.
Depicts submission on that day and the loss of fabricated claims.
States that punishment is increased for corrupting others.
Criminals see the Fire, know they will enter it, and find no escape.
Confirms that every attempted exit from the Fire returns them to it.
Links light scales with loss and abiding in Hell.
The condemned acknowledge that misery overcame them and led them astray.
Those in the Fire plead to be brought out, promising change.
The answer fixes their remaining in the Fire without further speech.
The wrongdoer regrets not having taken the messenger's way.
The wrongdoer regrets taking a particular companion as intimate ally.
Identifies that companion as turning him away from the reminder.
Places the condemned in dispute within the punishment scene.
Their confession names their manifest error.
They admit having equated others with the Lord of the worlds.
They identify criminals as those who led them astray.
Adds the loss of any devoted friend alongside absent intercession.
God calls the alleged partners whom they claimed.
They are called to their partners and wish they had been guided.
False mutual bonds turn into mutual denial and cursing, ending in Fire.
Repeats the refusal to leave ancestral following for divine revelation.
Criminals ask to return after seeing the truth and claim readiness to act.
Those in the Fire wish they had obeyed God and the messenger.
They explicitly blame leaders and great ones for misguidance.
They ask that those leaders receive doubled punishment and curse.
Rejecters state they will not believe, then appear before their Lord.
Arrogant leaders deny forcing the weak followers, exposing shared blame.
Weak and arrogant trade blame while both conceal remorse at punishment.
Describes enduring Fire for rejecters without death or reduction.
Identifies Hell as the promised destination of rejection.
Portrays the condemned turning on one another in questioning.
Followers accuse those before them of approaching from a position of influence.
Those blamed deny faithfulness and redirect culpability to the followers.
They deny coercive power and call the followers transgressors.
The misleaders admit leading others astray because they were astray.
Confirms their shared participation in punishment.
Denies that any earthly ransom could avert the evil punishment.
States that the evil of their deeds becomes apparent to them.
Counters the excuse of missed guidance with the arrival of God's signs.
Shows faces darkened for those who lied against God.
Depicts the weak disputing with the arrogant inside the Fire.
The arrogant deny any ability to remove punishment from followers.
Shows one who turns from the reminder assigned a devil companion.
Those companions obstruct the way while making it seem guided.
The follower wishes an immense separation from the companion when he arrives.
Denies that regret will benefit those who shared wrongdoing.
Shows close friends becoming enemies except the God-conscious.
Shows the evil of deeds becoming apparent and punishment enclosing them.
Describes calling upon beings unable to answer until the Day of Resurrection.
Those invoked become enemies and deny the worship given to them.
A companion disowns responsibility for the condemned person's transgression.
Satan commands rejection, then disowns the person who obeys him.
States the severe destination of Hell for those who reject their Lord.
The condemned admit that listening or reasoning would have spared them the Fire.
Their confession of sin confirms their remoteness from deliverance.
Begins the scene in which no close friend asks about another.
Shows the criminal wishing to ransom himself with his own children.
Extends the futile ransom wish to everyone on earth.
Rejects every ransom and names the blazing Fire.
The wrongdoer sees what his hands sent ahead and makes a final regretful wish.
Hell is brought near and the human being finally remembers.
Expresses regret at not sending ahead for one's real life.
